newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end mixed erasing early gains.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end mixed erasing early gains.

text.p: Israeli shares closed off their highs on Wednesday as investors took profits, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 0.03 percent, or 0.10 points, to 303.95 on an all-share turnover of 210 million shekels against 228 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.40 percent lower at 309.07.
Traders said that the session opened with mild gains following the rise of Israeli shares traded in New York. But by midday the trend changed and the market started falling.

"I don't know why the market lost momentum. The market is still strong and it seems that the positive trend will continue. The weakening might be a healthy correction," said Zvi Hoffman at Meitav Investments and Securities.
"I believe that this is only a mild correction as investors got nervous by the rapid rise of the market," said a trader at United Mizrahi Bank.

"Perhaps the reason for the change is that investors fear that the spending promises (Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu) has given to the coalition members would hurt the fiscal restraint," Hoffman said.
Israeli newspapers said on Wednesday that written promises given by Netanyahu to coalition partners, to defuse a government crisis, would cost the Treasury up to three billion shekels,

The agreements reached in the last month with Foreign Minister David Levy's Gesher faction and the Israel ba'Aliya immigrant party call for increased spending on education and a series of social causes.

The Mizrahi trader added that the market was also affected by high activity of Maof options speculators. "The Maof players were moving the market. In the next few days I believe that we will see more profit taking but the trend is still very positive," she said.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which rose 3.25 percent to 34,322 agorot on volume of 13.3 million shekels; Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which gained 0.25 percent to 23,527 on turnover of 11.8 million shekels; and Bank Leumi, which fell 0.25 percent to 570 agorot on turnover of 10.5 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
